full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, that the present petitioner as pre-emptor filed a pre-emption miscellaneous case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla against the opposite party No.1 as pre-emptee and others contending inter alia that the case joie is the ejinali homestead; wherein the petitioner and other co-sharers are residing with their family members. The opposite party No.2 transferred the case land in favour of the pre-emptee without serving any notice and without any information to the petitioner. For getting the land pre-empted the pre-emptor filed the pre-emption miscellaneous case within time. The further case of the pre-emptor is such that the purchaser-pre-emptee is a stranger to the case jote. 

 4. During pendency of the case the pre-emptee after making his appearance filed a written objection alleging that under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act; under which the pre-emptor have instituted the original pre-emption miscellaneous case is not maintainable and as such the pre-emption miscellaneous application is liable to be rejected under Order VII rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure along with other grounds therein. The learned trial Judge vide his order dated 24.05.2010 rejected the application for rejection of the plaint under Order VII rule 11(Gha) of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereafter, vide order dated 09.06.2010 opined that the pre-emption miscellaneous case is maintainable in its present form. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the grounds of the revisional application and the argument advanced from the side of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and submits that the learned lst revisional court was quite empowered to entertain the revisional application and committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that in fact the original pre-emption miscellaneous case was not maintainable under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 and the pre-emptor had no right to institute the original pre-emption miscellaneous case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act inasmuch as admittedly the pre-emptor is not the co-sharer by inheritance in the case joie and the learned 1st revisional court after proper appreciation of the connected law apprised that the matter is required to be decided under the purview of present law which is prevailing at the moment and apparently it is found that the petitioner have no locustandi to file such application for pre-emption and that's why the learned trial court had no other alternative but to dismiss the original case. The learned Advocate also submits that the case kabalas admittedly were executed on 07.07.2008 and 26.12.2007 and both the two cases for pre-emption were filed on 30.12.2008 which is long after the amendment of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951. The purchaser-pre-emptee-opposite party knowing about the institution of the original cases filed the application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for the aforesaid reason for rejection of plaint. But the learned trial court illegally disallowed the said application for rejection of plaint. The learned Advocate lastly submits that both the two cases were barred by law and thereby the learned revisional court was quite legal and justified in holding the view that the cases are liable to be dismissed. 

 11. On perusal of the papers it transpires that the present petitioner for having the case land pre-empted filed the pre-emption miscellaneous case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against the pre-emptee-opposite party on 30.12.2008. It is the case of the pre-emptor that he is the co-sharer by purchase in the case holding and by virtue of that capacity he has filed the pre-emption miscellaneous case against the stranger purchaser-pre-emptee. 

 13. Having gone through the connected papers I find that the learned revisional court i.e. the learned Judge (District Judge), Jananirapatta Bighnakari Aparadh Daman Tribunal, Comilla rightly held that, under the provision of law only the co-sharer by inheritance have locustandi to prefer pre-emption miscellaneous case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951. 

 State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 has been amended which has come into effect/force from 20.09.2006. 

 15. The law of pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has been amended by Act XXXIV of 2006. The former section 96 has been amended by the act of law and the right of pre-emption under the said section 96 now a days runs as follows: 

 17. Keeping ahead the submissions advanced form the side of the learned Advocates for the parties the learned 1st revisional court relying upon some decisions of the Apex Court reported in 18 DLR 709 and 716 invoking the inherent power of the Court and 8 BLC 144 with regard to applicability of section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the proceedings under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and 13 BLD (AD)56 with regard to the application under section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure, rightly decided the merit of the revisional application in the affirmative.
